title: One JSONL system: the five unchecked writers get the same check

message.text: Plan: one Sonnet minion closes the five gaps from the writer audit, in the audit's order — a Write/Edit hook that refuses an existing .jsonl (a new file is still allowed), schema checks in the browser's rpc:append and in ledger.mjs, a schema for flags.jsonl with the clarity skill pointed at append.mjs, and the new-task skill naming the route for day.jsonl. The standing rule holds: a guard never stops logging itself — ledger writes the line anyway and marks why it failed the check. Brief: /framework/ai/2026-10-02/jsonl-writers/requirements.md ($12).

All 5 unchecked JSONL writers are closed: a hand Write/Edit onto an existing .jsonl is blocked, the browser's rpc:append validates every line, ledger.mjs's writes can never go silent, flags.jsonl has a real schema, and new-task names its day.jsonl route. Two fresh-eyes reviews ran (one caught a real bug — a static import that could have taken the whole ledger down — now fixed); 75/75 tests pass. This landed as applied to michael/dev, not committed — merge.mjs 3-way-merged onto edits already uncommitted there, so the owner still needs to commit the touched files. Full detail and both reviews are in task.jsonl. One loose end I'm leaving alone: worktree qf-9 won't return to the pool cleanly because other agents' live, unrelated task logs sit uncommitted in it — not mine to touch or force through.

Landed and committed to michael/dev. Checked here, not taken on trust: 75 test checks pass across the four test files. What is now checked that was not: a Write or Edit into an existing .jsonl is refused (a new file still opens), the browser's rpc:append and the ledger hook run every line through the same schema check (the ledger writes the line regardless and marks why), flags.jsonl has a schema and the clarity skill writes it through append.mjs, and new-task names the route for day.jsonl. The Write/Edit guard applies to sessions started from now; rpc:append gets it when the dev server restarts, which I batch with the other pending restarts.
